## Purpose and Entry Points
FastAPI is a Python API framework built on Starlette’s ASGI layer and Pydantic’s type-driven validation/schema model. Its public library surface is exported from `fastapi/__init__.py`; application construction centers on `fastapi/applications.py`. Runtime invocation is available through `python -m fastapi` (`fastapi/__main__.py`) and the `fastapi` CLI (`fastapi/cli.py`), which discovers and serves user applications via Uvicorn.

## Application and Route Assembly
`FastAPI` configures an ASGI application, default exception handling, OpenAPI/docs endpoints, middleware, and lifespan behavior in `fastapi/applications.py`. Route declarations and router composition are implemented in `fastapi/routing.py`; `APIRouter` aggregates path operations, prefixes, dependencies, response defaults, callbacks, and webhooks before inclusion in an application. This is the main author-facing control boundary.

## Request Execution Pipeline
An HTTP or WebSocket request enters through Starlette/ASGI, then FastAPI route handlers in `fastapi/routing.py`. Handler construction inspects endpoint signatures, creates a dependency graph, extracts path/query/header/cookie/body/form/file data, validates it through Pydantic, invokes sync or async endpoints, and serializes the result. Concurrency adaptation is in `fastapi/concurrency.py`; request and WebSocket public types/wrappers are in `fastapi/requests.py` and `fastapi/websockets.py`.

## Dependency Injection and Parameters
Parameter marker types and declaration APIs live in `fastapi/params.py` and `fastapi/param_functions.py`. `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` converts annotations and defaults into dependency models, recursively resolves dependencies, caches results per request, handles security scopes, and manages yielded dependency cleanup. `fastapi/dependencies/models.py` holds the dependency graph representation. This layer is the bridge between Python signatures and request-time execution.

## Validation, Serialization, and Errors
FastAPI supports Pydantic v2 and compatibility behavior through `fastapi/_compat/v2.py` and `fastapi/_compat/shared.py`. It derives fields/schema information from type annotations, encodes arbitrary Python return values through `fastapi/encoders.py`, and applies response-model validation/filtering in routing. Framework exceptions and conversions to HTTP responses are defined in `fastapi/exceptions.py` and `fastapi/exception_handlers.py`; response classes are exposed in `fastapi/responses.py`.

## OpenAPI and Documentation Boundary
Route and model metadata are transformed into OpenAPI documents by `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`, using models/constants in `fastapi/openapi/models.py` and `fastapi/openapi/constants.py`. Documentation UI HTML for Swagger UI, ReDoc, and OAuth redirects is generated in `fastapi/openapi/docs.py`. The generated OpenAPI schema is both an API contract and source for interactive docs/client generators, distinct from request serving.

## Extension Surface and Protocol Support
The package layers FastAPI-specific integrations over Starlette: middleware adapters in `fastapi/middleware/`, static files and templates in `fastapi/staticfiles.py` and `fastapi/templating.py`, background tasks in `fastapi/background.py`, and server-sent events in `fastapi/sse.py`. Security scheme/dependency implementations span `fastapi/security/oauth2.py`, `fastapi/security/http.py`, and `fastapi/security/api_key.py`; they participate in both dependency resolution and OpenAPI generation.

## Repository Delivery Model
This is a Python package, not a deployed application. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` define the Python build/dependency environment. The project’s material external runtimes are Python, Starlette/ASGI, Pydantic, and optionally Uvicorn; optional runtime integrations include HTTPX, Jinja2, multipart parsing, and FastAPI Cloud through the CLI. Documentation is a separate multilingual publishing asset rooted at `docs/en/mkdocs.yml`, with executable examples under `docs_src/`.
